purpose: Fenfluramine is used to help reduce seizures in people who have a rare and serious type of epilepsy called Dravet syndrome. It is typically used along with other seizure medicines when other treatments have not worked well enough. It can significantly cut down how often seizures happen.
how_it_works: Fenfluramine works by increasing the activity of a brain chemical called serotonin, which helps calm down overactive electrical signals in the brain that cause seizures. It also activates certain receptors in the brain that help regulate nerve activity. Think of it as helping your brain's natural 'calm down' system work better to prevent seizures.
common_side_effects: Decreased appetite and weight loss, diarrhea, feeling tired or sluggish, drooling or increased saliva, low blood sugar (especially in people taking certain other seizure medicines), feeling unsteady or having trouble with coordination, and upper respiratory infections.
warnings: This medicine has a serious risk of causing heart problems, specifically damage to the heart valves and a condition called pulmonary arterial hypertension (high blood pressure in the lungs). Because of this, patients must have regular heart tests (echocardiograms) before and during treatment. Fenfluramine is only available through a special restricted program called the Fintepla REMS Program. It should not be used with other medicines that increase serotonin, as this can cause a dangerous reaction. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor.
typical_dosing: Dosing is based on body weight and is started at a very low dose, then slowly increased over time. The dose is taken by mouth twice a day. Your doctor will carefully calculate the right dose for you or your child and will adjust it gradually to find the best and safest amount.
